description:
A script taking a destination rejects an unrecognised option instead of treating it as the destination.

## Background

`scripts/assemble-package.sh` takes one positional argument, the destination, and parses no options. Invoking it as `./scripts/assemble-package.sh --help` therefore assembles the full package tree into a directory literally named `--help` in the current working directory, and reports success.

A run replaces its destination whole, so the same shape applied to a mistyped path is a directory-replacing write chosen by a typo.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: An argument beginning with `-` that the script does not recognise is a usage error, and nothing is written.
- [hard] REQ-02: `--help` prints usage and exits successfully without writing.
- [hard] REQ-03: Invoking the script with no destination, or with more than one, is a usage error naming what was expected.
- [hard] REQ-04: The existing single-destination invocation continues to work unchanged.
title: Reject an unrecognised option instead of writing to it
